texts.preamble: Mohit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 January, 2020 Author: Sunil Kumar Awasthi Bench: Sunil Kumar Awasthi
texts.facts: This first application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 has been filed by applicant, who is implicated in connection with Crime No.470/2019 registered at Police Station Neemuch Cant., Neemuch District Neemuch (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 272, 273 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. The applicant is in custody since 16.10.2019. As per prosecution case, on 06.09.2019, complainant Sanjeev Kumar Mishra s/o Late Purushottam Narayan Mishra, Food Security Officer made a written complaint against Chokanna Balaji Firm Baluram Hukimichand Garg, situated at Girls School Neemuch regarding adulteration in spices. On 28.07.2019 Officer of Food & Drugs Administration Department raided the aforesaid premises; and found substandard food products (spices). On the basis of the aforesaid complaint and raid by the Food & Drugs Administration Department, a case has been registered at Police Station Neemuch Cant., Neemuch, District Neemuch (MP) against the applicant for offence punishable under Sections 272, 273 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in the present crime. It is further submitted that if the allegation made in the FIR is taken on its face value or accepted in its entirety, then also not a single document is available on record, which shows the availability of ingredients for commission of offence under Section 420 of IPC in the present case. From the contents of the FIR, it appears that the applicant has violated the provisions of Food & Safety Standards Act, 2006. Learned Public Prosecutor for the non-applicant / State of Madhya Pradesh opposes the bail application by contending that no sufficient ground is made out for releasing the applicant on bail; hence he prayed for rejection of the application.
